blindSummary: The site of 2025 killings of trans women in this state/province. The national public prosecutor's study of LGTB homicides 2012–2021 identified 84 criminal complaints, 88 victims and 72 identified perpetrators, and found 58% of the deaths occurred in six fiscal districts, led by this state/province (12) and a sibling state/province (10), with one district among them; the central district also concentrates the highest national frequency of reported crimes overall (10.0%; eleven fiscal districts hold 62%). On 24–28 August 2025 a trans woman reported missing in a district of the state/province was found dead in her own home four days later; market colleagues and relatives publicly demanded justice. On the law side, congress approved a norm in February 2025 restricting trans people's access to public bathrooms — analysed by a national human-rights institute as 'legalised discrimination' — and a 2024 rights-observatory report counted 54 LGBTI+ murders 2020–2023, with trans women most affected.
blindSourceSummaries: A national news outlet (20 February 2025): congress approves a norm that strikes against trans people's right to use public bathrooms; interviews with an LGBTIQ rights activist describing the measure as an attack on trans people's access to public space.

A national university's human-rights institute bulletin ('legalised discrimination'): analysis of congress's prohibition on trans people accessing public bathrooms, characterised as legalised discrimination with public-space consequences.

An LGBT news agency (22 July 2024): hate crimes rose — 54 LGBTI+ people were murdered 2020–2023 according to the annual report of the LGBTI+ human-rights observatory of a national university, with trans women the most affected.
blindOutOfScope: The central district concentrates the highest national frequency of reported crimes overall (10.0%; eleven fiscal districts hold 62%) — general crime, not trans-specific; general crime and political instability affect all travellers.
